dervis-irab:1-5.t:
* Vocabulary:
(تَحِلَّةَ) a maṣdar (verbal noun) of حلّل with doubled [middle radical], like تكرمة; these two are not according to rule, for the regular maṣdar of [the pattern faʿʿala], when it is sound and without hamza [, is al-tafʿīl] [Translator's note: the source sentence is incomplete; the bracketed completion follows the evident sense]. As for the one whose final radical is weak, like زكّى, and the one whose final radical is hamza, like نبّأ, their maṣdars are تزكية and تنبئة; although al-tafʿīl has come in full in the weak verb, as in:
باتت تنزي دلوها تنزيا ... كما تنزي شهلة صبيا
(She spent the night jerking her bucket up and down, as an old woman jerks a child up and down.)
Its origin is تحللة, like تكرمة, and then [the two lāms] were assimilated.
(تَظاهَرا) with the second tāʾ of the original assimilated into the ẓāʾ, and in one reading without it [i.e. تظاهرا with lightening]; that is, "the two of you support one another".
(قانِتاتٍ) obedient.
(ثَيِّباتٍ) plural of ثيّب, from ثاب يثوب, i.e. he returned, as if she has returned [to her former state] after the loss of her virginity. Its origin is ثيوب, like سيّد and ميّت, whose origins are سيود and ميوت, and they underwent the phonetic change (iʿlāl) that will come in the section on benefits [Translator's note: so in the source; the section on benefits of this entry does not in fact treat it].

* I'rab:
(يا أَيُّهَا النَّبِيُّ لِمَ تُحَرِّمُ ما أَحَلَّ اللَّهُ لَكَ تَبْتَغِي مَرْضاتَ أَزْواجِكَ وَاللَّهُ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ) The i'rab of يا أيها النبي has been given many times. As for لم: the lām is a preposition and ما is an interrogative noun in the position of genitive by the lām; it has been mentioned before that when a preposition enters upon the interrogative ما its alif is dropped. The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) تحرم; ما is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause أحلّ الله is the ṣila (relative clause); لك is attached to أحلّ. The clause تبتغي is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of تحرم, and مرضاة أزواجك is the mafʿūl bihi. الله is a mubtadaʾ (subject), غفور the khabar (predicate) and رحيم a second khabar.
(قَدْ فَرَضَ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ تَحِلَّةَ أَيْمانِكُمْ) قد is a particle of realisation (taḥqīq); فرض الله is a verb and its fāʿil; لكم is attached to فرض; تحلّة is the mafʿūl bihi and أيمانكم muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), i.e. Allah has legislated for you the release from your oaths in the manner set out at length in the books of law.
(وَاللَّهُ مَوْلاكُمْ وَهُوَ الْعَلِيمُ الْحَكِيمُ) The wāw is a conjunction; الله is a mubtadaʾ and مولاكم the khabar; هو is a mubtadaʾ, العليم a first khabar and الحكيم a second khabar.
(وَإِذْ أَسَرَّ النَّبِيُّ إِلى بَعْضِ أَزْواجِهِ حَدِيثاً) The wāw is resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya); إذ is the mafʿūl bihi of an omitted verb, i.e. "remember"; the clause أسرّ النبي is in the position of genitive by the annexation of the adverb to it, and حديثا is the mafʿūl bihi.
(فَلَمَّا نَبَّأَتْ بِهِ وَأَظْهَرَهُ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ عَرَّفَ بَعْضَهُ وَأَعْرَضَ عَنْ بَعْضٍ) The fāʾ is a conjunction; لمّا is an adverb meaning "when", or a linking [particle] containing the sense of condition; the clause نبّأت is in the position of genitive by the annexation of the adverb to it. The basic rule for أنبأ, نبّأ, أخبر, خبّر and حدّث is that they take one object by themselves and a second by means of a preposition, which may be omitted. So you say نبّأت به, the first object being omitted, i.e. "someone other than her"; and من أنبأك هذا, i.e. بهذا; and he said نبّأني, i.e. نبّأني به or نبّأنيه. When they are made to include the sense of أعلم ("to inform"), they take three objects, as in the poet's saying:
نبئت زرعة والسفاهة كاسمها ... يهدي إليّ غرائب الأشعار
(I was informed that Zurʿa — and folly is as its name — is sending me strange poems.)
In the verse, نبّأت takes two objects, the first of which is omitted, and the second is genitive with the bāʾ, i.e. "she told it to someone other than her". As for وأظهره: the wāw is a conjunction; أظهره, i.e. He informed him, is a verb and a mafʿūl bihi, الله is the fāʿil, and عليه is attached to أظهره. The clause عرّف has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussivizing condition; بعضه is the mafʿūl bihi; أعرض is conjoined to عرّف, and عن بعض is attached to أعرض. The second object of عرّف is omitted, i.e. he made her know part of what she had done. In one reading it is عَرَفَ with the lightened form, i.e. he requited [it] with reproach and blame, as you say to someone who hurts you: لأعرفنّ لك ذلك, i.e. "I will certainly requite you".
(فَلَمَّا نَبَّأَها بِهِ قالَتْ مَنْ أَنْبَأَكَ هذا قالَ نَبَّأَنِيَ الْعَلِيمُ الْخَبِيرُ) The fāʾ is a conjunction; لمّا is temporal, meaning "when", or a linking [particle] containing the sense of condition in either case. نبّأها is a verb, a latent (mustatir) fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi; the clause قالت has no grammatical position. من is an interrogative noun in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ, and the clause أنبأك is the khabar; the kāf is a first object and هذا a second object. قال is a past verb, and the clause نبّأني العليم الخبير is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); العليم is the fāʿil of نبّأني and الخبير an adjective.
(إِنْ تَتُوبا إِلَى اللَّهِ فَقَدْ صَغَتْ قُلُوبُكُما) إن is conditional and تتوبا is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn; the alif is the fāʿil, and إلى الله is attached to تتوبا. The apodosis is omitted, its implied form being "He will turn to you [in forgiveness]". The fāʾ is causal; قد is a particle of realisation; صغت, i.e. inclined, is a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa implied on the alif that was dropped because of the meeting of two quiescents; the tāʾ is the quiescent tāʾ of the feminine, and قلوبكما is the fāʿil of صغت.
(وَإِنْ تَظاهَرا عَلَيْهِ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ مَوْلاهُ وَجِبْرِيلُ وَصالِحُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ) The wāw is a conjunction and إن is conditional; تظاهرا is the protasis, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn; the alif is the fāʿil, and عليه is attached to تظاهرا. The apodosis is omitted, its implied form being "he will find a helper". The fāʾ is causal; إنّ and its noun, هو is a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl), and مولاه is two khabars [Translator's note: so in the source, «خبران»; evidently for «خبرها» "its khabar"]; the pause is here. جبريل is a mubtadaʾ and صالح المؤمنين is conjoined to جبريل. صالح is a generic noun (ism jins), not a plural, and that is why it has come without a wāw after the ḥāʾ. They have permitted it to be a plural with wāw and nūn, the nūn being dropped for annexation, and written without the wāw in consideration of the pronunciation, since the wāw drops because of the meeting of two quiescents; but there is no need for this artificiality. You may also conjoin جبريل and صالح المؤمنين to the position of إنّ and its noun, so that the predicate of them all is مولاه; while on [the view of] its being a mubtadaʾ, the khabar is His saying ظهير, because in the pattern faʿīl the singular and the plural are the same, as has been mentioned before.
(وَالْمَلائِكَةُ بَعْدَ ذلِكَ ظَهِيرٌ) You may conjoin الملائكة to what precedes, or parse it as a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is ظهير; this has been pointed out already.
(عَسى رَبُّهُ إِنْ طَلَّقَكُنَّ أَنْ يُبْدِلَهُ أَزْواجاً خَيْراً مِنْكُنَّ) عسى is a past verb, one of the verbs of hope, and ربه is its noun. إن is conditional, and طلقكنّ is a past verb, a latent fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi, in the position of jussive as the protasis. أن is a maṣdar-forming and accusative particle; يبدله — with the lightened form, and it has also been read with doubling — is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by أن; أن and what falls within its scope are the khabar of عسى; the hāʾ is a first mafʿūl bihi. The apodosis is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, i.e. "then perhaps". أزواجا is a second mafʿūl bihi, خيرا an adjective, and منكنّ is attached to خيرا. The condition was placed between عسى and its khabar out of concern for the matter and to make them afraid.
(مُسْلِماتٍ مُؤْمِناتٍ قانِتاتٍ تائِباتٍ عابِداتٍ سائِحاتٍ ثَيِّباتٍ وَأَبْكاراً) مسلمات is a second naʿt (adjective) of أزواجا; it may also be parsed as a ḥāl, and some made it accusative by specification (ʿalā al-ikhtiṣāṣ), which is fine; what follows are multiple adjectives. The wāw was placed between ثيّبات and أبكارا because the two descriptions are mutually exclusive in this case, unlike the rest of the adjectives; it is not the "wāw of eight" (wāw al-thamāniya), as some have imagined. This has been discussed in detail before.

* Rhetoric:
He used the plural in His saying «قلوبكما», and this was permissible because it is annexed to a dual, namely the pronoun of the two of them. The plural in such a case is more frequently used than the dual; and the dual, [less] than the plural [Translator's note: the source's «والتثنية دون الجمع» "and the dual below the plural" evidently means the dual is less frequent than the plural], as the poet said:
فتخالسا نفسيهما بنوافذ ... كنوافذ العبط التي لا ترفع
(The two of them snatched each other's lives with piercing thrusts, like the piercing cuts in sound camels that are not mended.)
This was the regular rule, namely that a dual be expressed by a dual; but they disliked the combination of two duals, so they turned to the plural, because the dual is a plural in meaning. The singular is not permissible according to the Basrans except in poetry, as in:
حمامة بطن الواديين ترنمي ... سقاك من العز الفوادي مطيرها
(O dove of the hollow of the two valleys, coo! May the rainy one among the morning clouds water you.) [Translator's note: the source prints «العز الفوادي», evidently for «الغرّ الغوادي» "the white morning clouds".]
He means بطني ("the two hollows").

* Benefits:
The Messenger did not make the awe of prophethood a deterring barrier between himself and his wives; rather, by his gentleness and his friendliness he made them forget that they were addressing the Messenger of Allah, at certain times. So among them was one who would say to him in front of her father: "Speak, and say nothing but the truth"; and one who would argue back with him or be angry with him for the whole of her day; and one who reached a degree of boldness towards him that a man like ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, with his sternness, would hear of and marvel at, and he would be about to strike his daughter Ḥafṣa because she was bold as the other wives were bold. The following story is a true model of this sublime conduct. Most of the commentators said, in summary: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was alone with Māriya on ʿĀʾisha's day, and Ḥafṣa came to know of it, so he said to her: "Keep it secret; I have made Māriya unlawful for myself; and I give you the good news that Abū Bakr and ʿUmar will rule the affairs of my community after me." But she told ʿĀʾisha of it, and the two of them were close friends. It has also been said that he was alone with her on Ḥafṣa's day, and he placated her with that and asked her to keep it secret, but she did not keep it secret; so he divorced her and withdrew from his wives, and stayed twenty-nine nights in Māriya's house. It is related that ʿUmar said to her: "If there were any good in the family of al-Khaṭṭāb, he would not have divorced you." Then Jibrīl, upon him be peace, descended and said: "Take her back, for she fasts much and stands much in prayer, and she is one of your wives in the Garden."
It is also related that he drank honey in the house of Zaynab bint Jaḥsh, and ʿĀʾisha and Ḥafṣa agreed together and said to him: "We smell on you the smell of maghāfīr." Maghāfīr is the plural of mughfūr, with ḍamma, like ʿuṣfūr: a sweet gum with an unpleasant smell, exuded by a tree called al-ʿurfuṭ (with ḍamma on the undotted ʿayn and on the fāʾ), found in the Ḥijāz, which has a smell like that of wine. He ﷺ disliked that an unpleasant smell should be found on him, so he made honey unlawful [for himself].
Al-Zamakhsharī was audacious and used, concerning the Prophet ﷺ, language that it is not permissible to use and that is not palatable to quote. Ibn al-Munayyir answered him with a sound reply and analysed this "making unlawful" with fine analysis. We confine ourselves to quoting it, passing over the remaining numerous views. Ibn al-Munayyir said:
«What al-Zamakhsharī said about the Prophet ﷺ is fabrication and slander, and the Prophet is free of it. That is because making unlawful what Allah has made lawful is of two kinds. [First:] believing that the ruling of unlawfulness is established for it; this is equivalent to believing the ruling of lawfulness for what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has made unlawful, and both are forbidden and do not issue from those who bear the mark of faith; and if it did issue, it would strip the believer of the ruling and name of faith. The second: abstaining from what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has made lawful; and taking "making unlawful" in its bare [sense] is correct, because of His saying "And We had forbidden to him the wet-nurses before", i.e. We prevented, nothing more. It may be reinforced by an oath while believing in its lawfulness, and this is purely permissible. The verse is to be taken according to the second kind, and the sound interpretation supports it: the Prophet ﷺ swore by Allah that he would not approach Māriya, and when the verse was revealed he made expiation for his oath; and what indicates it is: "Allah has ordained for you the release from your oaths". This degree is permissible, and there is no sin in doing it. It was said to him "Why do you forbid what Allah has made lawful for you?" only out of gentleness towards him and compassion for him, and to exalt his standing and his rank ﷺ above having to consider the pleasure of his wives in what is hard on him, in accordance with what is familiar of Allah the Exalted's kindness to His Prophet and His raising him above being put out [Translator's note: the source prints «يخرج», evidently for «يحرج» "being put in difficulty"] on account of any of the human beings who are his followers and for whose sake they were created [Translator's note: so in the source; the intended sense is probably "for whose sake (i.e. the Prophet's) they were created"], so that Allah may show the perfection of his prophethood through the evidence of their falling short of him. Al-Zamakhsharī did not take "making unlawful" in this sense, because he made it a slip (zalla), and so takes it in the first sense. Allah forbid, and far be it from Allah! For even ordinary believers are far from believing unlawful what Allah has made lawful; so how could he not keep the rank of the Prophet above what even the rank of the common people of the community is raised above? This on al-Zamakhsharī's part is nothing but audacity towards Allah and His Messenger, speaking loosely without verification, and putting forward corrupt opinion without reflection».

dervis-irab:6-8.t:
* I'rab:
(يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا قُوا أَنْفُسَكُمْ وَأَهْلِيكُمْ ناراً وَقُودُهَا النَّاسُ وَالْحِجارَةُ) قوا is an imperative verb from al-wiqāya (protection), so its measure is عُوا, because the fāʾ [first radical] was dropped, as it occurs in the imperfect between a yāʾ and a kasra, and this [imperative] is modelled on that; and the lām [final radical] was dropped by analogy with the jussive. The explanation is that [the original is] أوقيوا [Translator's note: the source prints «أوقوا»; the full original form is أوقيوا], like اضربوا: the wāw, which is the fāʾ of the word, was dropped for the reason mentioned; the connecting hamza (hamzat al-waṣl) was dropped because the quiescent letter it introduced was dropped; the ḍamma on the yāʾ was found heavy and was dropped, so two quiescents met, and the yāʾ was dropped, and the letter before the wāw was given ḍamma so that it [the wāw] would be sound. The wāw is the fāʿil (agent), أنفسكم is a first mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and أهليكم is conjoined to أنفسكم, the sign of its accusative being the yāʾ because it is assimilated to the sound masculine plural. نارا is a second mafʿūl bihi. وقودها is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and الناس the khabar (predicate), or the reverse; الحجارة is conjoined to النار [Translator's note: so in the source; evidently for «الناس»]. The clause وقودها الناس is an adjective of نارا.
(عَلَيْها مَلائِكَةٌ غِلاظٌ شِدادٌ لا يَعْصُونَ اللَّهَ ما أَمَرَهُمْ وَيَفْعَلُونَ ما يُؤْمَرُونَ) The clause is a second adjective of نارا. عليها is a fronted khabar and ملائكة a postponed mubtadaʾ; غلاظ is a naʿt (adjective) of ملائكة and شداد a second naʿt. لا is negating; يعصون الله is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), its fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi. ما is maṣdariyya; أمرهم is a past verb, a latent (mustatir) fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi; ما with what it governs is interpreted as a maṣdar (interpreted maṣdar) in the position of accusative as a badal ishtimāl (substitute of inclusion) from الله, as if it were said "they do not disobey His command". Abū Ḥayyān permitted its being accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. "in what He commands them". As for ويفعلون: the wāw is a conjunction, and يفعلون is an imperfect verb, nominative, and its fāʿil; ما is a relative noun, the mafʿūl bihi, and the clause يؤمرون is the ṣila (relative clause), the returning pronoun being omitted, i.e. "[commanded] with it". Al-Zamakhsharī said: «If you ask: are the two clauses not of one meaning? I answer: no; for the meaning of the first is that they accept His commands and hold to them, and the meaning of the second is that they carry out what they are commanded, without being sluggish about it or slack in it». So a difference is established. As for al-Bayḍāwī, he answered this question by saying: «It has been said: they do not disobey Allah in the past, and they do what they are commanded in the future».
(يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لا تَعْتَذِرُوا الْيَوْمَ إِنَّما تُجْزَوْنَ ما كُنْتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ) لا is prohibitive; تعتذروا is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the prohibitive لا; اليوم is an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) تعتذروا. The clause is the object of an omitted saying, i.e. that will be said to them upon entering the Fire. إنما is [إنّ] made inoperative by [ما] (kāffa wa-makfūfa); تجزون is a passive imperfect verb, the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), and ما is a second mafʿūl bihi; the clause كنتم is the ṣila of ما, and the clause تعملون is the khabar of كنتم.
(يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا تُوبُوا إِلَى اللَّهِ تَوْبَةً نَصُوحاً) توبوا is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; إلى الله is attached to توبوا; توبة is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) and نصوحا a naʿt of توبة.
(عَسى رَبُّكُمْ أَنْ يُكَفِّرَ عَنْكُمْ سَيِّئاتِكُمْ) عسى is an inflexible (jāmid) past verb, one of the verbs of hope, and ربكم is its noun; أن and what falls within its scope are in the position of accusative as the khabar of عسى; عنكم is attached to يكفر, and سيئاتكم is the mafʿūl bihi.
(وَيُدْخِلَكُمْ جَنَّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهارُ) ويدخلكم is conjoined to يكفر; the kāf is a mafʿūl bihi and جنات a second mafʿūl bihi by extension (ʿalā al-saʿa); the clause تجري is a naʿt of جنات; من تحتها is attached to تجري, and الأنهار is the fāʿil of تجري.
(يَوْمَ لا يُخْزِي اللَّهُ النَّبِيَّ) The adverb is attached to يدخلكم, or to an omitted verb whose implied form is "remember", in which case it would be a mafʿūl bihi. لا is negating; يخزي الله is an imperfect verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is in the position of genitive by the annexation of the adverb to it; النبي is the mafʿūl bihi.
(وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا مَعَهُ نُورُهُمْ يَسْعى بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَبِأَيْمانِهِمْ) The wāw may be a conjunction, with الذين in the position of accusative, conjoined in sequence to النبي; then نورهم is a mubtadaʾ and the clause يسعى the khabar, and the clause is new (mustaʾnafa) or circumstantial. Or the wāw may be resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya), with الذين a mubtadaʾ and the clause نورهم يسعى its khabar. As for بين أيديهم, the adverb is attached to يسعى, and بأيمانهم is conjoined to the adverb and attached to what it is attached to.
(يَقُولُونَ رَبَّنا أَتْمِمْ لَنا نُورَنا) The clause is a second khabar or circumstantial. ربنا is a one addressed (munādā) in a genitive construct (muḍāf); the vocative clause, together with the imperative verb after it, its fāʿil and its object, is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
(وَاغْفِرْ لَنا إِنَّكَ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ) Conjoined to what precedes.

* Rhetoric:
1- In His saying «توبة نصوحا» there is figurative attribution (isnād majāzī): sincerity is attributed to the repentance figuratively, whereas it really belongs to the one repenting, for hyperbole. Its like has preceded many times.
2- In His saying «لا يعصون الله ما أمرهم ويفعلون ما يؤمرون» there is a wonderful figure which they have called "negation and affirmation" (al-salb wa-l-ījāb). It is building speech upon negating a thing from one aspect and affirming it from another, or commanding a thing from one aspect and forbidding it from another aspect; it has been discussed before. In the verse it is clear: He, Mighty and Majestic, negated disobedience of these described beings and affirmed obedience for them. If it is said: on the apparent sense of this verse there is a difficulty in terms of overlap and repetition, for the meaning of its end is included in the meaning of its beginning, so it is repeated even though its wording differs, and this is a defect from which the composition of the Mighty Book is kept free, since whoever does not disobey obeys — I have not seen anyone address this difficulty and answer it except the Imām Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī, who said: «They do not disobey Allah in the present, and they do what they are commanded in the future»; and that is, in any case, an answer that does not resolve the difficulty, which rather remains. Ibn Abī al-Iṣbaʿ answered by saying:
«Description in terms of obedience and disobedience is of three kinds. You say: Zayd does not disobey and obeys; its opposite: he does not obey and disobeys; and the intermediate: he does not disobey and does not obey. The first is the highest description, the second the lowest, and the third the middle. The Real, Glorified is He — and He knows best — wished to describe these angels with the highest description. Had He, Mighty and Majestic, confined Himself to His saying "they do not disobey", it would have been possible for it to be continued with your saying "and they do not obey", and that would not fulfil the intended meaning, since what is intended is to describe them with the highest of descriptions. So it was necessary for Him to say "and they do", so that the description is complete. And Allah knows best».
Al-Zamakhsharī raised this difficulty and answered it as follows: «If you ask: are the two clauses not of one meaning? I answer: no; for the meaning of the first is that they accept His commands and hold to them, and do not refuse them or reject them; and the meaning of the second is that they carry out what they are commanded, without being sluggish about it or slack in it. If you ask: Allah has addressed the idolaters who deny the revelation with exactly this, in His saying, the Exalted: "But if you do not, and you never will, then fear the Fire whose fuel is people and stones", and He said: "prepared for the disbelievers", so He made it prepared for the disbelievers; what then is the meaning of His addressing the believers with it? I answer: the grave sinners (al-fussāq), even though their levels are above the levels of the disbelievers, dwell together with the disbelievers in one abode; so it was said to those who believe: protect yourselves, by avoiding grave sin, from dwelling with the disbelievers for whom this described Fire has been prepared. It is also possible that He commands them to guard against apostasy and against regretting having entered Islam». [Translator's note: the source does not mark the end of the quotation; it evidently ends here.]
Ibn al-Munayyir al-Mālikī followed it up in his book al-Intiṣāf, saying: «His first answer is derived from his corrupt principle of believing that grave sinners abide eternally in Hell. Perhaps he raised the question only so as to strain to give an answer to it that would vent what is in himself of this falsehood which he cannot bear to conceal».

dervis-irab:9-12.t:
* Vocabulary:
(وَاغْلُظْ عَلَيْهِمْ) be severe with them in speech, and let no leniency or softness take hold of you in dealing with them. In al-Qāmūs: «الغلظة, with the three vowels [on the ghayn], and الغلاظة with kasra, and like ʿinab [i.e. غِلَظ], is the opposite of softness; the verb is like karuma and ḍaraba, so he is غليظ, and غُلاظ like ghurāb; أغلظ له في القول: he was rough with him in speech».

* I'rab:
(يا أَيُّهَا النَّبِيُّ جاهِدِ الْكُفَّارَ وَالْمُنافِقِينَ وَاغْلُظْ عَلَيْهِمْ) The i'rab of يا أيها النبي has been given many times. جاهد is an imperative verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "you"; الكفّار is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and المنافقين is conjoined to الكفّار. اغلظ is an imperative verb conjoined to جاهد, and عليهم is attached to (mutaʿalliq) اغلظ.
(وَمَأْواهُمْ جَهَنَّمُ وَبِئْسَ الْمَصِيرُ) The wāw is resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya); مأواهم is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and جهنم the khabar (predicate). بئس is an inflexible (jāmid) past verb for expressing blame, المصير is the fāʿil, and the one specified for blame (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm) is omitted, i.e. "it".
(ضَرَبَ اللَّهُ مَثَلًا لِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا امْرَأَتَ نُوحٍ وَامْرَأَتَ لُوطٍ) A new (mustaʾnaf) statement set out to present a strange case, so that in its light another strange case, resembling it in strangeness, may be understood.
ضرب الله is a verb and its fāʿil; مثلا is a fronted second mafʿūl bihi, and the lām with its genitive is attached to an omitted adjective of مثلا; امرأة نوح is the first mafʿūl bihi, and امرأة لوط is conjoined to امرأة نوح.
(كانَتا تَحْتَ عَبْدَيْنِ مِنْ عِبادِنا صالِحَيْنِ فَخانَتاهُما) The clause is new, set out to explain the striking of the parable. كان is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb, the tāʾ is the quiescent tāʾ of the feminine, and the alif is the noun of كان; as for تحت عبدين, the adverb is attached to an omitted khabar of كان; من عبادنا is a naʿt (adjective) of عبدين. فخانتاهما is conjoined; it is a past verb, its fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi. The names of the two women and their story will come in the section on benefits.
(فَلَمْ يُغْنِيا عَنْهُما مِنَ اللَّهِ شَيْئاً وَقِيلَ ادْخُلَا النَّارَ مَعَ الدَّاخِلِينَ) The fāʾ is a conjunction; لم is a particle of negation, inversion [of tense] and jussive; يغنيا is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لم, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn; the alif is the fāʿil, and عنهما is attached to يغنيا; من الله is a ḥāl (circumstantial), and شيئا is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) or a mafʿūl bihi. وقيل is conjoined to what precedes; it is a passive past verb, and the clause ادخلا is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); النار is a mafʿūl bihi by extension (ʿalā al-saʿa), and مع الداخلين is an adverb attached to ادخلا. The past verb قيل is imperfect in meaning, i.e. "and it will be said to them".
(وَضَرَبَ اللَّهُ مَثَلًا لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا امْرَأَتَ فِرْعَوْنَ إِذْ قالَتْ رَبِّ ابْنِ لِي عِنْدَكَ بَيْتاً فِي الْجَنَّةِ) Conjoined to what precedes. إذ is an adverb attached to مثلا; perhaps it is better to say that it is attached to an omitted badal (substitute) from مثلا. The clause قالت is in the position of genitive by the annexation of the adverb to it. ربّ is a one addressed (munādā) in a genitive construct (muḍāf), with the vocative particle omitted; ابن is an imperative verb of supplication, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the weak letter, and لي is attached to ابن. عندك is an adverb attached to an omitted ḥāl of the first-person pronoun, or of بيتا, because it precedes it. في الجنة is an ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) or a badal of His saying عندك, or is attached to ابن.
(وَنَجِّنِي مِنْ فِرْعَوْنَ وَعَمَلِهِ وَنَجِّنِي مِنَ الْقَوْمِ الظَّالِمِينَ) ونجّني is conjoined to ابن, and من فرعون is attached to نجّني; عمله is conjoined; من القوم is attached to نجّني, and الظالمين is a naʿt of القوم.
(وَمَرْيَمَ ابْنَتَ عِمْرانَ الَّتِي أَحْصَنَتْ فَرْجَها فَنَفَخْنا فِيهِ مِنْ رُوحِنا) ومريم is conjoined to امرأة فرعون; ابنة is a badal or naʿt of مريم; عمران is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct) [Translator's note: the source says «مضاف»], made genitive with fatḥa because it is a diptote, on account of being a proper name and having the added alif and nūn. التي is a naʿt of مريم, and the clause أحصنت فرجها is the ṣila (relative clause) of التي, i.e. she guarded it and protected it from men. فنفخنا is conjoined to أحصنت; فيه is attached to نفخنا; من روحنا is an adjective of an omitted mafʿūl bihi, i.e. "a spirit from Our spirit", من being partitive. The meaning of the blowing has been discussed earlier.
(وَصَدَّقَتْ بِكَلِماتِ رَبِّها وَكُتُبِهِ وَكانَتْ مِنَ الْقانِتِينَ) وصدّقت is conjoined to something omitted and implied, suited to the context, i.e. "so she conceived ʿĪsā and believed". بكلمات is attached to صدّقت, and ربها is muḍāf ilayhi; كتبه is conjoined to كلمات. كانت is a defective past verb whose noun is latent, its implied form being "she", and من القانتين is the khabar. Two views are possible regarding من: first, that it is for the beginning of the extent (ibtidāʾ al-ghāya); second, that it is partitive, the masculine being used by way of predominance (taghlīb).

* Rhetoric:
In the striking of the parable there is an allusion (taʿrīḍ) to Ḥafṣa and ʿĀʾisha, mentioned at the beginning of the sūra, and to their lapse in supporting one another against the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in what he disliked; and a warning to them in the harshest and severest manner, given that the parable mentions disbelief and the like; and an indication that it is their duty to be, in sincerity and in keeping it secret, like these two believing women, and not to rely on being the wives of the Messenger of Allah, for that merit will not benefit them unless they are sincere. The allusion is to Ḥafṣa because Lūṭ's wife disclosed his secret, just as Ḥafṣa disclosed the Messenger of Allah's secret. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: «In the two parables there is a lesson for the wives of the Prophet ﷺ, since their reproach came earlier; but this is far-fetched, because the text being about the disbelievers makes this unlikely».

* Benefits:
The commentators mentioned that Nūḥ's wife used to tell his people that he was mad, and her name was Wāhila, with the hāʾ before the lām, and it has been said the reverse; and that Lūṭ's wife used to guide his people to his guests when they lodged with him, by night by lighting a fire and by day by making smoke, and her name was Wāʿila, with the ʿayn before the lām, and it has been said the reverse. As for Pharaoh's wife, her name was Āsiya bint Muzāḥim, and she had true insight regarding Yūsuf [Translator's note: so in the source; the story — "a comfort of the eye for me and for you" (al-Qaṣaṣ 28:9) — concerns Mūsā, not Yūsuf] when she said: "a comfort of the eye for me and for you". Among her merits is that she chose being killed over kingship, and the torment of this world over the luxury in which she used to live.
Moreover, there is consensus that the wife of a prophet never committed fornication. It has been said that their betrayal was hypocrisy, and it has been said that they betrayed them by tale-bearing.
